clue.text: Wading bird stopped over halfway in difficulty — one might go in for a dip

definitions.text: one might go in for a dip

indicators.note: the bird's name is cut off once more than half of it has been written, losing its last two letters

parts.note: the avocet is a long-legged wading bird with an upturned bill
ado is fuss or trouble, as in 'without further ado'

explanation.surface: A wader got stuck partway through something tricky, and then the clue swerves to a dinner-party dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped over halfway' cuts AVOCET to AVOC, four of its six letters. Guacamole, a popular dip, is made from this fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is the base of guacamole, so it is something a person dips into, a playful description.

clue.text: Person standing for president is the seat of corruption?

parts.note: vice is moral corruption or wickedness
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A presidential candidate is mocked as the throne of corrupt dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing for' means deputising, not running for office; 'seat of corruption' reads as the answer's two parts in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy who substitutes for the person presiding over a meeting holds this title.

clue.text: Daily help Independent's left with electronic word puzzle

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British term for a cleaning lady

indicators.note: the letter for Independent has gone away, left the word

parts.note: aid means help
I is the abbreviation for Independent
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A cleaner from the Independent's office departs to build an electronic word game.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British cleaning woman who comes in daily; 'left' removes I from AID, giving AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A party game in which a word is guessed syllable by syllable from mimed scenes is a puzzle about words.

clue.text: Filthy hound in a film

parts.note: filthy means dirty
to hound someone is to harry or harass them

explanation.surface: A mucky dog appears in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hound' looks like a dog but is a verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1971 Clint Eastwood police thriller is a famous movie.

clue.text: Criminal lost bet and chickens out

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or bent, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook loses a wager and runs away instead of paying up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle it is British slang for losing one's nerve, the same as being too scared to go on.

clue.text: Self-referentially concealed in the past?

indicators.note: the word concealed both signals hiding and is itself the word the letters are hidden in

explanation.surface: A clue that hides something about itself, asking what happened long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue word 'concealed' contains the answer, and also tells you it is concealed there.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly or at one time, this adverb refers to an earlier period.

clue.text: I am European, into everything French for a short break

indicators.note: the letters go inside the French word

parts.note: tout is French for all, everything
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A European diving into all things French, but only for a quick holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause in play, or a brief rest from activity, is called by this phrase.

clue.text: Bar is out of cordial at both ends — it makes you weep

indicators.note: the selected letters are taken out of the word for bar

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word cordial are taken

explanation.surface: A warm-hearted host bans someone from the bar, and it brings tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at both ends' picks C and L from cordial; 'is out of' removes them from EXCLUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wounds or walls that weep ooze liquid slowly, which is to seep or discharge.

clue.text: Pissed off about one religious service or made more religious?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the other pieces
the word pissed is turned off its normal course into a rearranged form

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a ritual is a ceremonial religious rite

explanation.surface: A drunk storms out of church, or is that a conversion experience?
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles PISSED to SPISED, which 'about' wraps round IRITUAL. 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a spiritual character is to make it more concerned with the soul and devotion.

clue.text: Basic food keeps a lecturer going back for tasty cake?

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is read backwards
the grain word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: rice is a staple food for much of the world

explanation.surface: A staple dish holds a teacher's attention as the teacher returns for a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts A L inside RICE to make RIALCE; 'going back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: This choux pastry filled with cream is a classic patisserie item, a delicious small cake.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink for when you're legless?

definitions.text: Alcoholic drink for when you're legless?

parts.words: Alcoholic drink for when you're legless?
parts.note: legless is British slang for very drunk, but read literally someone with no legs would need lifting, so the drink is a reviver

explanation.surface: A tipple to have when you have already had far too many.
explanation.walkthrough: A restorative drink, often a hair of the dog, is taken to perk someone up; a person without legs would literally ask to be lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic or stiff drink that revives a person is known by this phrase, which literally asks to be raised.

clue.text: Where bangers end up measured in metric?

definitions.meaning: bangers is British slang for old, worn-out cars, which go to be broken up
when lengths are given in metric units the imperial yard is abandoned, scrapped

explanation.walkthrough: Bangers here are old cars, not British sausages. The second reading splits the answer as 'scrap yard': ditch the imperial unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cars are taken to a breaker's yard for dismantling; going metric means the old imperial measure is discarded.

clue.text: Was on a horse beside the ring here?

definitions.text: Was on a horse beside the ring here?

indicators.note: one piece sits next to the other in the answer

parts.note: rode is the past tense of ride
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone recalls riding next to the arena at a cowboy show.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the event: people rode horses around the arena there.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest where riders sit broncos in an arena is exactly where people rode by the ring.

clue.text: Ordinary members inform and encourage society

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone to the police
to root for someone is to cheer them on

explanation.surface: Members of a club tell tales and spur the society on.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass is British slang for telling tales to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank and file of a party or movement, rather than its leadership, are called this.

clue.text: Head of state's mature wise man

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to age is to mature, grow older

explanation.surface: A nation's leader is described as a grown-up man of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of great learning and judgment, a philosopher, is the noun meaning of this word.

clue.text: Without aid for housing start getting unsettled — sacrifices to be made here

indicators.note: the solo word contains the other letters, as a house holds its occupants

parts.note: to do something alone is to do it unassisted

indicators.note: the letters of start are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone working unaided finds their start upset, and sacrifices must follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without aid' is the synonym ALONE, not an instruction to drop letters; 'getting unsettled' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Offerings were placed on the stone slab of an altar, the place where victims were offered to a god.

clue.text: Escort vulnerable girl after chap is replaced by unfeeling boss

indicators.note: one word is swapped out of the escort's title for another

parts.note: a chaperone accompanies and protects a young woman
the word chap is spelt out literally in the escort's title
numb means without feeling

explanation.surface: A young woman's escort is dropped for a cold-hearted man in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The escort's title begins with the word chap; swap it for NUMB.
explanation.definitionFit: The top person, the chief, is informally referred to as the leader at the head of the ranking.

clue.text: Nothing to stop angry radicals in decisive moment

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry

indicators.note: the zero plugs a gap within the other word, stopping it up

parts.note: rads is a short informal word for radicals
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing will hold back furious extremists at this turning point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' puts O inside RADS, giving ROADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a junction of paths is an idiom for a crucial point where a choice must be made.

clue.text: Cleaner uniform worn by Vardy perhaps?

indicators.note: the letter is inside the footballer word, as clothes are within a wearer's outfit

parts.note: Jamie Vardy is an English footballer known for scoring goals, an example of a striker who nets goals
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cleaner's overall is the kit a footballer might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamie Vardy is an English Premier League striker, so 'Vardy perhaps' is a goal scorer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad or powder used for scrubbing pans is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Chalky substance in two sorts of tree

definitions.meaning: quicklime is calcium oxide, made from chalk or limestone
the linden is called by this name, as is the citrus tree bearing green fruit

explanation.walkthrough: One word names two unrelated trees: the linden and a citrus.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium oxide, a white powder from burnt limestone, and both the linden and a citrus tree share this name.

clue.text: Hero's mate is new in directorial role

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for the director's role

parts.note: a leader directs others, a role of direction

explanation.surface: A star's partner is the newcomer in charge of the film.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Hero was a priestess whose lover swam the Hellespont nightly to her; 'Hero' looks like a film star but is her name.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the young man who swam to the priestess Hero was her lover and partner.

clue.text: Son goes to a supermarket to get some ice cream

parts.note: the Co-op is a British cooperative chain of supermarkets

explanation.surface: A boy is sent to the shops to buy a little ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a long-established British supermarket chain run as a cooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball of ice cream served with a spoon-like tool is a portion, some of the dessert.

clue.text: Take top off? This is a good laugh, taking top off

indicators.note: the first letter is removed, the top of a down answer

parts.note: something hilarious is called a scream

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hilarious to keep taking their top off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition: to skim off the best part, the top layer of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim off the best, as the top layer of milk is taken, is a verb sense of this dairy word.

clue.text: One needs to watch what one says

definitions.text: One needs to watch what one says

parts.words: One needs to watch what one says
parts.note: the phrase usually means a careful speaker, but here the person literally looks at the speaker's mouth to follow speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'watch what one says' is an idiom for speaking carefully; taken literally it describes someone who follows speech by sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person who understands speech by observing mouth movements must literally watch spoken words.

clue.text: Rob's first to be out for a duck

indicators.note: the opening letter is dismissed, out like a batsman

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A cricketer called Rob is first out, and for zero runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This small freshwater dabbling bird is a species of duck.

clue.text: Spare salesman always turns up when first person goes in

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative

indicators.note: the pronoun is inserted into the reversed word
in a down light the word for always is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman keeps showing up as soon as someone enters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses EVER to REVE, and 'goes in' puts I inside to give RIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare a condemned person is to grant them a stay of execution or pardon.

clue.text: Likely lad with no partner?

parts.note: an odd sock or glove is one without its pair
a son is a boy, a lad

explanation.surface: A probable lad who is single.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a horse at shorter odds than evens is favoured to win, hence probable.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting term for a favourite expected to win, so a result that is probable.

clue.text: Gemstone redeemer sees 50% off all cut diamonds

indicators.note: the first half of the word's letters are taken away, leaving the back four
the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A saviour finds half price on every cut stone in a jeweller's sale.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' leaves EMER from REDEEMER, and 'cut' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: This green precious stone, a variety of beryl, is a gem.

clue.text: Cold war powers one pitted against every leader of new regime

indicators.note: the pieces are set next to each other
the second of the two powers has its middle stones removed, like pitted fruit

parts.note: the two Cold War superpowers were the US and the USSR
per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: Superpowers set against each other and every new government's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one pitted' strips the middle SS out of USSR, leaving UR after US.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes power wrongfully heads the regime that replaces the lawful one.
